Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin 2 is a desktop 3D-printing slicer (a fork of OrcaSlicer, C++ with wxWidgets and two React pages; repository `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin`, public on GitHub) with its own server in the private tsd-enterprise repository. A person chats with an AI in the app through a JusPrin account, where the server's gateway forwards the chat to an AI provider and charges credits, or with their own key for OpenAI, OpenRouter or Anthropic. They also connect their own printers, save projects, keep a print history, send print reports and buy credits through Chargebee. Over November 2026 the error handling was reworked twice and got it wrong in opposite directions, as the task describes. On 2026-11-24 a real report showed the pattern again: a person's OpenRouter workspace was restricted to their own provider keys, OpenRouter's answer said so in plain words with a link, and the app said "Something went wrong on our side" and filed a report. Kenneth's point was that this failure is one only the person can act on, and that the questions to ask of any failure are common sense: can the person understand it, can they act on it, can we do anything about it, and is it a bug in our code. The error-handling rules were then rewritten around one idea, and he judged that understanding good enough. Three code readers, given only the new text, read the app and the server and produced the list of 42 cases; six were confirmed by a second read, none was run, and no reader reached every file (the gaps are named at the end of the list). The app reports to the developers through `report_unexpected_error` and `report_if_automatic` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`), sent by Sentry's native SDK, and only when the person presses "Report to JusPrin team" or has automatic reports on. The server reports through Sentry's Django integration and the gateway's own top handler. Kenneth wants reports in plain language for a reader who did not see the work: full sentences, no made-up labels, decisions asked as full "Decision needed" paragraphs, proposals marked as proposals, and inference marked as inference.

Task:
Fix the places where JusPrin sends a failure to the wrong one. The list is `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/error-handling-misrouted-failures.md` (an untracked working file; do not commit it): 42 numbered cases in the desktop app and the JusPrin 2 server, each with a file and line.

**Read the rule first.** It is the "Error handling" section of `AGENTS.md` in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin` (branch `jusprin-dev`) and of `CLAUDE.md` in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise` (branch `master`). The current text opens with "Someone pastes a key from their own AI service". If the copy you read does not open that way, the new text has not landed on that branch yet: read it in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/error-rules-whose` of each repository, and say so in your first report. Its one idea: a failure has to reach whoever can do something about it, in a form they can use. A failure that is the person's reaches them in words they can understand, true about where the problem lies, with what to do next, and in the other side's own words when those were written for a person; it is not reported. A failure that is ours reaches us with everything the code knew, the person is told only that it is not their fault, and the work stops. A failure nobody here can fix, such as a service the person chose being down, is told to the person truthfully and not reported. When it cannot be told whose a failure is, it comes to us.

**Do not repeat the two earlier mistakes.** JusPrin 2.0.0 told the person "the service could not be reached" for failures that were ours, and nobody heard of them. JusPrin 2.0.1 swung the other way: it told the person "Something went wrong on our side" for failures only they could fix, and filled Sentry with reports nobody could act on. Both came from sorting by code path, status code or a prepared list of cases, not by looking at the failure and asking whose it is. So for each case, read what the other side really says, decide whose it is, and fix the branch for "anything else" so the next unlisted failure of the same kind also goes the right way. Adding one more recognised answer and one more sentence to a list is not a fix. Add no classification tables.

**Questions that are Kenneth's. Ask them at the start, each as a full "Decision needed" paragraph with the options and what each costs, and carry on with what does not depend on them.**
1. How the app shows the other side's own words. One way for every case, for example the service's name followed by its message. He approves that once; after that, showing a service's words needs no approval per case.
2. Every new sentence of ours. Collect them into one list with where each appears, and bring him the list; do not ask one at a time. A sentence of ours needs his yes, quoted in the commit message.
3. The situations the rule does not settle, listed at the end of the working file: whether work that failed must be undone (case 41, a message charged although the AI provider failed); whether a failure retold by the AI model counts as reaching the person; what "the work stops" means for a background save that retries; what the person is told when a report cannot be sent.
4. Case 27 is JusPrin 1's server code. Leave it alone unless he says otherwise.

**Order.** Start with the two cases about money (41 and 42), then the cases a person is most likely to meet. Each group in the working file says which direction the failure goes wrong.

**How to work.**
- Kenneth's rule: never fix what you have not reproduced. Every case in the list comes from reading only, and several are marked inferred. For each, first show the wrong behaviour in the real app or server (a scratch copy of the app with its own data folder, never Kenneth's running JusPrin; the one local server stack that exists, never a second), then fix it, then show the right behaviour. Where a case depends on how an outside service answers, verify that from the service's own documentation or a real answer, not from memory. If a case cannot be made to happen, change nothing for it and say so.
- A failure that is ours gets no handling code: it is thrown where it is found, keeping the other side's status, request id and error text, and the one handler at the top of the entry point reports it. Every failure, whoever it goes to, is also written to the log.
- Send nothing to a real Sentry project. Spend nothing on real AI services without asking Kenneth first.
- JusPrin: new branches from `jusprin-dev` in worktrees under `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/`; never check `jusprin-dev` out in a worktree. tsd-enterprise: work in a worktree under its `.claude/worktrees/`, because other sessions share the main checkout; never stage `obico-server` or `.claude/launch.json`.
- New sentences must be translatable and added to the catalogs as the repository's localization rules say.
- Commit only when Kenneth asks, push only when he asks, no attribution lines. Builds on this Mac are shared: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`, build with `-- -j4`, one build per build directory.
- This is a long task. Work through it in groups you can finish and show, and report after each group rather than at the very end.

**Done looks like:** for each of the 42 cases, one of: reproduced, fixed and shown fixed, with a test; shown not to happen, with the evidence, and left unchanged; or waiting on a named decision of Kenneth's. Report in plain language: what the person saw before and sees now, what we received before and receive now, what you tested, and what is still open.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_cd3120f7-030a-4af8-a6d1-28ecae789f1a

# Failures that go to the wrong one

Found on 2026-11-24 by three code readers who were given only the new error-handling write-up
("a failure has to reach whoever can do something about it, in a form they can use") and asked to
find every place the code does not do that. App code read on `origin/jusprin-dev` (110a9492e0),
server code on `origin/master` of tsd-enterprise. Everything is by reading; nothing was run.
"Checked" marks the cases a second reader confirmed against the code. None of the readers reached
every file; what they did not reach is at the end.

App paths are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Server paths are under `web_ent/jusprin/`.

## A. Ours, but the person is told it is theirs or the network's, and we never hear of it

App
1. Credits and plans, Billing and usage. `Shell/ServerSheet.cpp:86-97, :215`. A server fault or an ended sign-in shows "Couldn't load Credits and plans. Check your internet connection, then try again." Checked.
2. Email sign-in. `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:314-315`. Any refusal the app has no branch for, and no network, both show "JusPrin couldn't sign you in. Try again." Checked.
3. Password sign-in. `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:312-313`. Any 400 becomes "That password is wrong." without reading the server's code.
4. Delete account. `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:153-159`, `AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:296`. Any failure shows "The account couldn’t be deleted. Check your internet connection, then try again."; status and body are dropped unlogged. Checked.
5. The app's own 120-second limit on a reply, a reply cut mid-stream, or one over 16 MiB. `Agent/AgentTransport.hpp:27-28`, `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:779-782`. Shows "The AI request could not reach the … service." Checked.
6. Print report with no answer (our server down, TLS failure, a large photo timing out). `Home/PrintHistory.cpp:250`, `HomeUI/src/components/PrintReportForm.tsx:139`. Shows "The report couldn't be sent. Check your connection and try again."
7. Update check. `Updates/UpdateCheck.cpp:104-136`, `AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:609`. GitHub answers 403 or 404, or a list the app cannot read: "Couldn't reach GitHub", which is untrue.
8. AI panel will not start. `Agent/AgentWebView.cpp:206, :237-241, :325-332, :372-389`; `AgentUI/src/App.tsx:83-87, :391-394`. Shows "The AI panel could not connect", "The AI page did not complete the bridge handshake." and "Bridge traffic: … sent / … received". Log only.
9. Home will not start. `Home/HomeWebView.cpp:80, 85, 177`. "The packaged Home page is missing from this build.", "The system web view could not be created.", "The Home page failed to load." Log only. The second may be a system part the person must install, and it does not say so.
10. JusPrin model list. `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:51-60`, `AgentUI/src/components/AgentConnection.tsx:142`. Our server answers a 4xx, or no network: "Signed in · AI unavailable … Try again in a moment." Only a 5xx is reported.
11. Browser sign-in. `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:346-348`, `Agent/CloudSignInMachine.cpp:93-104`. Another program holds the port, or our token exchange fails: "Signing in didn't finish. Nothing was saved. Try again." Log only.
12. Autosave. `Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:351`, `Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:166-185`, `Shell/StatusRow.cpp:430, :615-616`. Disk full, folder not writable, or our bug all show "Couldn't save … JusPrin will retry." The system's reason is dropped, so it cannot be told whose it is.
13. Export, restore, version history. `Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp:144-146, :161-168, :184-187`. "The project couldn't be exported. Try again." and two like it; reason logged only.
14. Opening a project. `Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:863, 922-954`, `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1446`. Open in a second window, the current project unsaved, or a damaged project: "The project couldn't be opened. Try again." Three owners, one sentence.
15. A saved project that cannot be read gets no card on Home. `Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:757`, `Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:443`. One cause is permanent: an interrupted chat restore leaves a marker that "requires recovery", and no code recovers it.
16. Projects folder unreadable. `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1017`. "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying."; the system's reason is dropped.
17. Profiles shipped with the app fail to install or read. `Home/OrcaImporter.cpp:231, 342`, `PrinterSetup/SetupOptionsLoader.cpp:85`. "JusPrin couldn't load this preset. …" Log only.
18. Save on a proposal card. `AgentUI/src/components/ProposalCard.tsx:31-32`. "The action failed."
19. Tool failures in the app's own work. `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:714-717`. They reach us only with automatic reports on.
20. The local tool server's helper. `Mcp/Bridge/Bridge.cpp:119, 163`. Any failed probe tells the outside AI client "Open JusPrin and a project, then try again.", even while JusPrin is open.
21. Ends in a log line or nothing: the history cleanup warning (`Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:455`); a damaged printer-facts file emptied without a log line (`Workspace/PrinterFactsStore.cpp:56-80`); a kept G-code file that changed (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1246`); a dropped file the page cannot read (`HomeUI/src/App.tsx:218`, `AgentUI/src/App.tsx:311-314`); an unreadable OrcaSlicer.conf read as "no printers" (`Home/OrcaImport.cpp:67`); a print-host test that throws (`PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:895`, inferred); a report that cannot be sent (`Support/SentryClient.cpp:89-93`).

Server
22. The app sends something the server refuses (a field a newer app added, a model removed from the aliases, an empty alias setting). `v2/errors.py:72-76`, `v2/gateway.py:206-211`, `v2/upstream.py:58-131`, `v2/views.py:172-175, 267-270`. Told "The request is not valid." or "This model is not available." We get one log line with the code only.
23. A paid Chargebee event that matches nothing (customer id without the `jusprinv2-` prefix, plan id missing from settings, unknown event). `ledger/billing.py:372-373, 377, 382`, `v2/views.py:104-106`. The credits never appear; silent return or bare 400.
24. Guesses in billing. `ledger/billing.py:154-157`: any Chargebee failure reads as "no card on file". `:168-173`: "subscription not found" on account deletion is taken as nothing to end. `ledger/reports.py:31-32`: any database conflict becomes "This print already has a report."
25. Browser session gone at checkout or on return from paying. `v2/web.py:301-302, 310, 319-321`. A silent redirect to Credits and plans after they paid.
26. Deactivated account or wrong-scope token told "Sign in to JusPrin to continue." (`v2/auth.py:18-22`); deactivated account or lost cache entry told "This link has expired" (`v2/views.py:203-208`).
27. JusPrin 1 code: `jusprin_cb_views.py:105-113` (user not found returns 200, nothing logged), `:168-175` (a bare catch drops the Obico discount), `:60-61` (a cancelled checkout raises a 500), `views.py:67-70`.

## B. The person's, but they are told "Something went wrong on our side" and we get a report

28. Own key: the service names a cause (country, moderation, key spending limit, no access to the model). `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:825-842, :793-796`; key check at `AgentUI/src/components/AgentConnection.tsx:411`. OpenAI or OpenRouter 403, 404 or 400.
29. Export G-code from Print history to an SD card that is full, locked or unplugged. `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1335`, thrown at `Shell/GcodeHistoryRecorder.cpp:454`. A dropped file that cannot be written (`:1496`) and a photo that cannot be read (`:1360`) take the same path.
30. Unreadable attachment (permission denied, drive gone). `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:1622-1637`.
31. Sign out with no network. `Agent/CloudSignInMachine.cpp:188-193`. Checked.
32. An AI tool exports to a folder that cannot be written. `Workspace/OrcaOutputs.cpp:363-411`, `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2690, 2825`. Coded "failed", so it is reported; for 3MF, STL and presets the reason is dropped.
33. Server: a provider refuses the person's own content. `v2/gateway.py:323-330, 352-354`. Inferred; not confirmed which providers answer this way.

## C. Reaches the right one, in a form they cannot use

34. Own key, HTTP 429. `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:751-755, :839-840`. "The OpenAI service is rate limited. Try again shortly."; the service's own words, which may name a daily cap, are dropped.
35. Too large, no next step. `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:757-761`. "The request was too large for the … service." does not say to start a new chat or remove pictures.
36. A Klipper printer's Moonraker answers 401 (key needed), or a proxy answers 502. `Printers/HostLaneReader.cpp:70`, sentence at `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:316`. "192.168.1.42:7125 isn't answering." It answered and refused.
37. Printer window. `Home/PrinterWindow.cpp:111, 167-182`. Any web view error that is not a certificate one: "Nothing answered at %s. Check that the printer is turned on…"
38. Server: a renewal's card is declined. `ledger/billing.py:290-294`, `v2/web.py:177-185`. Told "This message needs 1 credit; you have 0." while the page says the plan is renewing.
39. Server: a report photo in HEIC format, or the server failing to read the upload. `v2/views.py:233-239`. One answer for both: "That photo could not be read."

## D. Neither's, but called ours

40. Own key: the service is down or overloaded. `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp` as in 28, in-reply `:501-506`, the model list (`Agent/ModelCatalog.cpp:197-201`), and a chat-title request after a good reply (`Agent/AgentHost.cpp:3491-3506`).

## E. A failure recorded as a success

41. Server: the AI provider fails after the message was charged. `v2/credits.py:55`, `ledger/ledger.py:123`, `v2/gateway.py:191-195`. The person is told "our side" and we get a report, but the charge stands and Billing and usage counts the message. No code gives credits back. Checked. Not checked: whether the app's retry reuses the turn id, which would make the retry free for an hour.
42. Server: a checkout returns "succeeded" with the invoice unpaid. `ledger/billing.py:347-351`. Told "500 credits added" though nothing was granted. Inferred that Chargebee can return this.

## What the write-up could not decide

- Whether work that failed must be undone (case 41).
- Whether a failure retold by the AI model, or handed to an outside AI client, counts as reaching the person (cases 18, 19, 20).
- What "the work stops" means for a background save that retries every few seconds (case 12).
- What the person is told when the report itself cannot be sent, or when they decline to send it.
- Whose failure it is when strangers post rubbish to a public address of the server (`v2/launches.py:34-40` sends it to Sentry).
- A service we chose but cannot change, such as GitHub for the update check (case 7).

## What the readers did not reach

- App: `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`, `Agent/ToolResults.cpp`, most of `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`, `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp` (about 150 of 3,845 lines read), `Canvas/`, `Startup/`, `PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp`, `PrinterCatalog.cpp`, `PrinterDiscovery.cpp`, parts of `HomeUI` and `Mcp/`, and all tests.
- Server: tests, most templates, allauth's own views.

## Error handling

Someone pastes a key from their own AI service, and the service refuses it because of a setting in their account. Only they can change that setting. Later the app loses a chat because of a mistake in our code. Only we can fix that. Every failure is like one of these: there is someone who can do something about it, and error handling is the work of getting the failure to them, in a form they can use.

A failure that is the person's has to reach them in words they can understand, saying truthfully where the problem lies and what to do next. When the other side, meaning the service, printer or system that refused, has already said this in words written for a person, show those words and say who said them, because it knows the situation better than a sentence we prepared. Two causes that leave the person doing the same thing share one sentence, since a second sentence tells them nothing more. Nothing is wrong with the app itself, so it carries on.

A failure that is ours has to reach us with everything the code knew, because we will have to find the cause. The person can do nothing with that detail. They need to know only that the fault is not theirs, and to have a way to send it to us. We write no code to deal with such a failure. Its cause is something we did not understand when we wrote the code, so any handling would be a guess, and a guess carries on in a state nobody can vouch for and hides the failure. The work stops.

Sending a failure to the wrong one is the mistake this section exists to prevent, and it can be made in both directions. Tell the person the service could not be reached when our server failed, and they check their network while we never hear of it. Tell them something went wrong on our side when their own account is out of credits, and they wait for us while our reports fill with things we cannot fix, until the ones we can fix are hard to see.

So look at the failure itself, with what the other side actually said, and work out whose it is. Usually it says. What we have prepared does not change the answer: a failure that is the person's stays theirs when nobody wrote a sentence for it. When it truly cannot be told, it comes to us, because a report we cannot use costs us one look, while a failure of ours that only the person saw is lost.

Sometimes that someone is neither the person nor us. A service the person chose, such as the AI service their own key is for, is down, overloaded or failing on its own side: whoever runs it can fix it, and nobody here can. The person still needs the truth, that the trouble is at that service and not with them or with JusPrin, so they stop looking for something to fix. It is not reported, because a report is for someone who can act on it. Behind a JusPrin account the AI service is ours, because we chose it and can change it, so its failures come to us.

A failure we know people will meet is part of the feature, and the feature is not finished until the person who meets it is told what to do. Every failure is also written to the log, whoever it goes to. The log is where we look when a report or a question sends us looking. It tells nobody anything by itself.

### In practice

- Whose a failure is depends on its cause, such as "out of credits" or "no network", both of them the person's. A status code, an exception type, or the way the failure arrives (an HTTP status, an event inside a reply) is not a cause.
- A branch for "anything else" decides for every failure nobody listed. A failure the other side says is the person's goes to the person, and one that cannot be told comes to us. One sentence there for failures with different owners is a guess.
- A sentence we write for the person needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message. Each has a test, and each time it is shown is counted. Showing the other side's own words needs no sentence of ours.
- A failure that is the person's, or that nobody here can fix, is handled with normal control flow, not exceptions, and is not reported.
- A failure that is ours gets one sentence, "Something went wrong on our side", and a way to report it. Do not sort such failures into kinds for the person, and do not bring Kenneth a question about the wording of one. On 2026-11-16 the code that kept five "try again" sentences apart was deleted for this reason.
- A failure that is ours stops the work and travels up unchanged. Do not catch it, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own.
- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Once it is clear that it is ours, or that it cannot be told whose it is, turn it into a thrown error on the spot and keep the other side's status, request id and error text.
- One handler at the top of each entry point reports through `report_unexpected_error` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`) and tells the person. No other code reports. In the code, a failure that comes to us is called unexpected, and any other is called expected.
- The report carries the other side's status, request id and error text, and the request's own facts, such as the user, the chat, the turn and the model.
- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is ours.
- One exception to "the work stops" and "no other code reports": a tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, its error goes to the AI model, and the turn goes on. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's mistake, it is also reported, with no dialog, and for this kind of failure only if the person has turned automatic reports on.
- Never record a failure as a success.

### Catching

- Catch a failure only when the code knows what it is and can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.

### Checks

- An agent reads the changed code against this section. Of each failure the code decides on, with what the other side really says, it asks: whose is it, and does it reach them in a form they can use?

"""Per-turn admission: rate limit, then the turn's charge in the credit ledger.

A turn is everything the client sends for one reply, including tool-call
follow-ups; every request of it carries the same X-JusPrin-Turn value. A turn
pays its model's price once, however many requests it makes. Title requests are
free, and a request of kind "note" is a turn the app started, not the person.

The reply requests of one turn are sequential (a follow-up is built from the
previous answer), so the charge does not guard against two reply requests of
the same turn racing each other.
"""
import enum
import time

from django.conf import settings

from jusprin.ledger.ledger import charge_turn
from jusprin.ledger.models import CreditCharge
from lib.cache import REDIS

KEY_PREFIX = 'jusprin:v2'
TURN_TTL_SECONDS = 60 * 60


class Admission(enum.Enum):
    ADMITTED = 'admitted'
    RATE_LIMITED = 'rate_limited'


def admit(user_id: int, turn_id: str, request_kind: str, alias, chat_id: str = None) -> Admission:
    """Count a new turn against the rate limit, then charge it once unless it
    is a title. Raises ledger.CreditsExhausted when it cannot be paid.
    Synchronous: Redis and the credit tables are both blocking."""
    seen_key = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:seen:{user_id}:{turn_id}'
    if REDIS.set(seen_key, '1', nx=True, ex=TURN_TTL_SECONDS):
        bucket = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:turns:{user_id}:{int(time.time() // 60)}'
        pipe = REDIS.pipeline()
        pipe.incr(bucket)
        pipe.expire(bucket, 120)
        turns_this_minute, _ = pipe.execute()
        if turns_this_minute > settings.JUSPRIN_V2_TURNS_PER_MINUTE:
            # The turn was not admitted, so its retry is a new turn again.
            REDIS.delete(seen_key)
            return Admission.RATE_LIMITED

    if request_kind == 'title':
        return Admission.ADMITTED

    charged_key = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:charged:{user_id}:{turn_id}'
    if not REDIS.set(charged_key, '1', nx=True, ex=TURN_TTL_SECONDS):
        return Admission.ADMITTED
    origin = CreditCharge.APP if request_kind == 'note' else CreditCharge.PERSON
    charged = False
    try:
        charge_turn(user_id, turn_id, alias, origin, chat_id)
        charged = True
    finally:
        # Only a turn that actually paid is remembered as paid, whether the
        # credits ran out or the credit tables raised.
        if not charged:
            REDIS.delete(charged_key)
    return Admission.ADMITTED

# Before you start: read the dev docs

Before doing any dev work in this project, read the root `README.md` and `obico-server/CONTRIBUTING.md`. They document the dev process that is NOT obvious from the code and that you are expected to follow, including:

- **Dependencies:** declare packages in `obico-server/backend/Pipfile` and regenerate `requirements.txt` with pipenv. Do NOT edit `requirements.txt` directly.
- **Pull requests:** open PRs against obico-server's `master` branch, not `release`.
- **i18n:** a UI change that adds or edits a `$t('...')` string is not complete until all frontend locale files (`obico-server/frontend/src/i18n/locales/`) are synced. See the README's "Frontend i18n" section.

# Error handling

Someone pastes a key from their own AI service, and the service refuses it because of a setting in their account. Only they can change that setting. Later the app loses a chat because of a mistake in our code. Only we can fix that. Every failure is like one of these: there is someone who can do something about it, and error handling is the work of getting the failure to them, in a form they can use.

A failure that is the person's has to reach them in words they can understand, saying truthfully where the problem lies and what to do next. When the other side, meaning the service, printer or system that refused, has already said this in words written for a person, show those words and say who said them, because it knows the situation better than a sentence we prepared. Two causes that leave the person doing the same thing share one sentence, since a second sentence tells them nothing more. Nothing is wrong with the app itself, so it carries on.

A failure that is ours has to reach us with everything the code knew, because we will have to find the cause. The person can do nothing with that detail. They need to know only that the fault is not theirs, and to have a way to send it to us. We write no code to deal with such a failure. Its cause is something we did not understand when we wrote the code, so any handling would be a guess, and a guess carries on in a state nobody can vouch for and hides the failure. The work stops.

Sending a failure to the wrong one is the mistake this section exists to prevent, and it can be made in both directions. Tell the person the service could not be reached when our server failed, and they check their network while we never hear of it. Tell them something went wrong on our side when their own account is out of credits, and they wait for us while our reports fill with things we cannot fix, until the ones we can fix are hard to see.

So look at the failure itself, with what the other side actually said, and work out whose it is. Usually it says. What we have prepared does not change the answer: a failure that is the person's stays theirs when nobody wrote a sentence for it. When it truly cannot be told, it comes to us, because a report we cannot use costs us one look, while a failure of ours that only the person saw is lost.

Sometimes that someone is neither the person nor us. A service the person chose, such as the AI service their own key is for, is down, overloaded or failing on its own side: whoever runs it can fix it, and nobody here can. The person still needs the truth, that the trouble is at that service and not with them or with JusPrin, so they stop looking for something to fix. It is not reported, because a report is for someone who can act on it. Behind a JusPrin account the AI service is ours, because we chose it and can change it, so its failures come to us.

A failure we know people will meet is part of the feature, and the feature is not finished until the person who meets it is told what to do. Every failure is also written to the log, whoever it goes to. The log is where we look when a report or a question sends us looking. It tells nobody anything by itself.

## In practice

- Whose a failure is depends on its cause, such as "out of credits" or "no network", both of them the person's. A status code, an exception type, or the way the failure arrives (an HTTP status, an event inside a reply) is not a cause.
- A branch for "anything else" decides for every failure nobody listed. A failure the other side says is the person's goes to the person, and one that cannot be told comes to us. One sentence there for failures with different owners is a guess.
- The server reaches the person through the desktop app: a named answer, which the app turns into a sentence. The named answers are the entries of `EXPECTED` in `web_ent/jusprin/v2/errors.py`, each with its cause, what the person sees and what they can do next. A new entry needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message. Each has a test, and each time it is given is counted.
- A failure that is the person's, or that nobody here can fix, is handled with normal control flow, not exceptions, and is not reported.
- A failure that is ours gets one sentence, "Something went wrong on our side", and a way to report it. Do not sort such failures into kinds for the person, and do not bring Kenneth a question about the wording of one. On 2026-11-16 the code that kept five "try again" sentences apart was deleted for this reason.
- A failure that is ours stops the work and travels up unchanged. Do not catch it, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own.
- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Once it is clear that it is ours, or that it cannot be told whose it is, turn it into a thrown error on the spot and keep the other side's status, request id and error text.
- One handler at the top of each entry point reports to Sentry and answers "Something went wrong on our side": the AI gateway's top handler calls `sentry_sdk.capture_exception` with the request's facts, and the Django views report through Sentry's Django integration. No other code reports. In the code, a failure that comes to us is called unexpected, and any other is called expected.
- The report carries the other side's status, request id and error text, and the request's own facts, such as the user, the chat, the turn and the model.
- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is ours.
- Never record a failure as a success.

## Catching

- Catch a failure only when the code knows what it is and can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.

## Checks

- An agent reads the changed code against this section. Of each failure the code decides on, with what the other side really says, it asks: whose is it, and does it reach them in a form they can use?
- To audit a commit range, use the `error-handling` skill in the JusPrin repository (`.claude/skills/error-handling/`). To check production for a period, use the `jusprin-production-check` skill (`.claude/skills/jusprin-production-check/`).

def record_subscription(user, sub: Dict) -> None:
    """Keeps the account's plan as Chargebee reports it, and grants the current
    term's credits once. A term of another plan on the same subscription (a
    switch) ends the earlier plan's lots: the days left on it come off the new
    plan's first payment."""
    plan, _ = JusPrinPlan.objects.get_or_create(user=user, defaults={
        'external_id': sub['id'], 'external_user_id': sub['customer_id'], 'plan_id': plan_price_id(sub)})
    plan.external_id = sub['id']
    plan.external_user_id = sub['customer_id']
    plan.plan_id = plan_price_id(sub)
    plan.current_term_start = _when(sub.get('current_term_start'))
    plan.current_term_end = _when(sub.get('current_term_end'))
    plan.billed_cents = billed_cents(sub)
    plan.obico_discount = has_obico_coupon(sub)
    status = sub.get('status')
    if status == 'cancelled':
        plan.expired_at = _when(sub.get('cancelled_at')) or timezone.now()
    elif status == 'non_renewing':
        # Cancelled at the end of the term: it ends when the term does.
        plan.expired_at = plan.current_term_end
    elif status in LIVE_STATUSES:
        plan.expired_at = None
    plan.save()

    if status not in LIVE_STATUSES or not plan.current_term_start or not is_v2_plan(plan.plan_id):
        return
    # A term is granted once it is paid. A renewal whose card failed, or a
    # switch not yet paid for, has an unpaid invoice until payment_succeeded
    # records the subscription again.
    if sub.get('due_invoices_count'):
        return
    term_ref = _term_ref(plan)
    made = _grant(user.id, CreditGrant.SUBSCRIPTION, settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS[plan.plan_id]['credits'], term_ref,
                  _lot_end(plan, 0))
    lots = CreditGrant.objects.filter(user=user, source_ref__startswith=f"term:{sub['id']}:")
    if not made:
        # A switch back to a plan this term already granted gives its lots
        # back, and a term whose end moved moves its lots' ends with it.
        for lot in lots.filter(source_ref__startswith=term_ref):
            lot.expires_at = _lot_end(plan, _month_of(term_ref, lot.source_ref))
            lot.save(update_fields=['expires_at'])
    now = timezone.now()
    lots.filter(expires_at__gt=now).exclude(source_ref__startswith=term_ref).update(expires_at=now)


def _pack_count(invoice: Dict) -> int:
    return sum(int(line.get('quantity') or 0) for line in invoice.get('line_items') or []
               if line.get('entity_type') == 'charge_item_price'
               and line.get('entity_id') == settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK_PRICE_ID)


def record_pack_invoice(user, invoice: Dict) -> int:
    """Grants the credit packs a paid invoice bought; the credits granted now,
    0 when they were granted before or the invoice isn't paid."""
    packs = _pack_count(invoice)
    if not packs or invoice.get('status') != 'paid':
        return 0
    credits = packs * settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK['credits']
    return credits if _grant(user.id, CreditGrant.PACK, credits, f"invoice:{invoice['id']}", None) else 0


def finish_checkout(user, hosted_page_id: str) -> Optional[Dict]:
    """Records what a finished checkout bought, when Chargebee sent the person
    back: 'pack' and the credits, or 'plan' and its id. None for a checkout the
    person cancelled: Chargebee sends a cancel to the cancel URL that the site's
    Hosted Pages settings choose, which may be this one. Chargebee sends a
    checkout back to the redirect URL only once it succeeded, so any other
    state, or a checkout that is not this account's, raises."""
    page = chargebee.HostedPage.retrieve(hosted_page_id, env=_site()).hosted_page
    if page.state == 'cancelled':
        return None
    if page.state != 'succeeded':
        raise RuntimeError(f'Checkout {hosted_page_id} came back {page.state}')
    content = page.content
    subscription = getattr(content, 'subscription', None)
    invoice = getattr(content, 'invoice', None)
    bought = (subscription if subscription is not None and is_v2_plan(plan_price_id(subscription.values)) else
              invoice if invoice is not None and _pack_count(invoice.values) else None)
    if bought is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f'Checkout {hosted_page_id} bought neither a JusPrin 2 plan nor a pack')
    if bought.customer_id != customer_id(user):
        raise RuntimeError(f'Checkout {hosted_page_id} is customer {bought.customer_id}\'s, '
                           f'not {customer_id(user)}\'s')
    if bought is subscription:
        record_subscription(user, subscription.values)
        return {'kind': 'plan', 'plan_id': plan_price_id(subscription.values)}
    record_pack_invoice(user, invoice.values)
    return {'kind': 'pack', 'credits': _pack_count(invoice.values) * settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK['credits']}


def retrieve_event(event_id: str) -> Optional[Dict]:
    """The webhook event with this id as JusPrin 2's site has it, or None when
    the site has no such event."""
    try:
        return chargebee.Event.retrieve(event_id, env=_site()).event.values
    except chargebee.InvalidRequestError as e:
        if getattr(e, 'api_error_code', None) != 'resource_not_found':
            raise
        return None


def handle_event(cb_event: Dict) -> None:
    """A webhook event from JusPrin 2's site; one about anything but a JusPrin 2
    plan or credit pack changes nothing."""
    content = cb_event.get('content') or {}
    event_type = cb_event.get('event_type')
    if content.get('subscription') and event_type in SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS | INVOICE_EVENTS:
        user = user_for_customer(content['subscription'].get('customer_id'))
        if user is None:
            return
        # Chargebee may send events late, twice or out of order, so the
        # subscription is read as it is now, not as the event saw it.
        sub = chargebee.Subscription.retrieve(content['subscription']['id'], env=_site()).subscription.values
        if is_v2_plan(plan_price_id(sub)):
            record_subscription(user, sub)
    elif event_type in INVOICE_EVENTS:
        invoice = content.get('invoice') or {}
        user = user_for_customer(invoice.get('customer_id'))
        if user is not None and not invoice.get('subscription_id'):
            record_pack_invoice(user, invoice)

- **Hosted page states:** Chargebee's docs say that when a hosted page reaches the "succeeded" state, the checkout's subscription, customer, card, and invoice resources can be fetched. A "cancelled" page carries no checkout information. (If hosted page state is "succeeded", then the subscription, customer, card & invoice(optional) resources during checkout can be obtained. If hosted page is state is "cancelled", then it will be empty)
- **One-time checkout flow:** The API reference describes the flow: you create the hosted page, the customer pays, and then you retrieve the page to get the invoice details. (Once they complete checkout, the non-recurring addons and one-time charges are automatically invoiced against the respective customer record.) Chargebee also recommends listening for webhooks such as invoice_generated to confirm a successful checkout.
- **Direct debit invoice status:** For a one-time direct debit payment, Chargebee creates a payment-due invoice tagged as payment initiated. (When a direct debit payment is initiated against a customer (and this holds for both one-time payments and recurring payments), a payment due invoice with a payment initiated tag is created in Chargebee.) The invoice is then marked paid or not paid based on a webhook from the payment gateway. (Chargebee is notified of the change in the status of the payment (via webhook) and consequently marks the invoice as either paid (for a successful payment) or not paid (for a failed payment).)
- **Timing:** Direct debit has a waiting period. (This waiting period is typically from three to four business days (five, if the mandate needs to be verified - in the case of a first payment or a one-time payment).) This likely explains why the hosted page can show "succeeded" while the invoice is still pending.

I didn't find documentation for an `in_progress` status on a hosted page or invoice, so verify that value against the API's enum list or a live response before relying on it. The most reliable approach is to treat the hosted page as succeeded, then read the invoice and its payment status, and use webhooks to track the final paid or failed outcome.

# Decisions needed from Kenneth: fixing failures that go to the wrong one (2026-11-24)

Session: "fix misrouted failures", working through the 42 cases in
`/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/error-handling-misrouted-failures.md`. Everything below is a question,
not something agreed. Where I say "my pick", that is a proposal.

## Decision needed: how the app shows a service's own words

Someone has their own OpenRouter key, and their OpenRouter workspace is set to use only their own
provider keys. OpenRouter answers the app's request with a message written for a person: "No endpoints
found that can be served by your own provider keys. This workspace is restricted to BYOK capacity. Add
provider keys at https://openrouter.ai/workspaces/default/byok". That is the real answer behind Sentry
issue JUSPRIN-APP-E today. The rule says to show those words and say who said them. I need one way to do
that, which you approve once, so that each new case needs no sentence of its own. The same form would be
used for an AI service, a printer's Moonraker or OctoPrint, and the operating system (for example "No
space left on device" when a save fails).

Options:
- (a) The service's name, then its words in quotation marks, alone: `OpenRouter says: “No endpoints
  found … Add provider keys at https://openrouter.ai/…”`. One translatable frame (`%1% says: “%2%”`);
  the words stay in the language the service wrote them in, usually English. Costs nothing more.
- (b) A sentence of ours first, then the service's words on a second line ("OpenRouter refused the
  request. It says: …"). Needs a sentence of ours per kind of refusal, which is what the rule tries to
  avoid.
- (c) The service's words with only a small label above them naming the service. Needs a design for the
  label in every place an error shows (chat card, Check key, printers, save status).

My pick is (a). The app would show only the service's message text, not the codes or metadata around
it; links in it stay as text. Is (a) the form you want?

## Decision needed: a message charged although the AI service failed (case 41)

Today the server charges a message's credits before it asks the AI service. If the AI service then fails
(down, overloaded, or our own fault), the person sees "Something went wrong on our side" and we get a
report, but the charge stays and Billing and usage lists the message. Nothing gives the credits back. I
also checked the app: pressing Retry sends the message under a new turn id (`AgentHost.cpp:3280`
appends "-attempt-N"), so the retry is charged again. The rule says "Never record a failure as a
success", but does not say whether failed work must be undone.

Options:
- (a) Give the credits back. When the request to the AI service fails on our side, the gateway's top
  handler, after reporting it, deletes that turn's charge and returns the credits to the lots they came
  from, so Billing and usage no longer lists it. Cost: about 30 lines in the ledger and gateway with
  tests; a person whose reply failed half-way through gets that partial reply free.
- (b) Keep the charge but mark it failed in Billing and usage. Cost: a new state and wording on the
  billing page; the person still pays for nothing.
- (c) Leave it as it is. Cost: people pay for replies they never got, and pay again on Retry.

My pick is (a), for a reply that ended in a failure that is ours. Do you want failed messages refunded?

## Decision needed: does the AI retelling a failure count as reaching the person?

When a tool call fails, its error text goes to the AI model, which then tells the person in its reply.
The rule already says how that failure reaches us (reported only with automatic reports on). What it
does not say is whether the model's retelling counts as the person being told, for a failure that is
theirs. Example: the AI exports a 3MF to a folder the person cannot write to (case 32); the tool's error
goes to the model, which may or may not pass on "permission denied". A related case: an outside AI
client (such as Claude Desktop) calls JusPrin's local tool server while JusPrin is open, and is told
"Open JusPrin and a project, then try again" (case 20).

Options:
- (a) Yes, it counts, provided the tool's error text says truthfully whose the failure is and carries the
  other side's words (for example the system's "Permission denied" and the folder). Cost: only the error
  texts change; we rely on the model to pass them on.
- (b) No: a failure that is the person's is also shown in the app outside the chat. Cost: a new place in
  the UI for it, and a design.

My pick is (a). Does a tool error that the model retells count as reaching the person?

## Decision needed: what "the work stops" means for autosave, which retries every few seconds (case 12)

Autosave writes the project every few seconds. When a write fails, the app shows "Couldn't save …
JusPrin will retry." and drops the system's reason, so neither the person nor we can tell why. If the
disk is full or the folder is read-only, it is the person's to fix; if the failure is our bug, it is
ours. The rule says a failure that is ours stops the work.

Options:
- (a) When the system says it is the person's (disk full, permission denied, read-only), show the
  system's words and keep retrying, so the save succeeds once they free space. For any other failure,
  report it once, stop autosaving that project for this run of the app, and show "Something went wrong
  on our side" with the way to report. Cost: autosave stops until restart for failures that are ours.
- (b) Keep retrying in every case, but report a failure that is ours once per project per run. Cost: the
  app goes on writing in a state nobody can vouch for, which the rule warns against.

My pick is (a). Which should autosave do?

## Decision needed: what the person is told when the report itself cannot be sent

The person presses "Report to JusPrin team" (or has automatic reports on), and the report cannot be sent,
for example with no network. Today it ends in a log line (`Support/SentryClient.cpp:89-93`).

Options:
- (a) Tell nobody, but keep the report on disk and send it at the next start. Cost: I have not yet
  checked whether our transport keeps unsent reports; if not, about 40 lines.
- (b) Tell the person "The report couldn't be sent." Cost: a new sentence; they can do nothing with it
  except try again.

My pick is (a). Which do you want?

## Decision needed: two cases the rule does not place

- Strangers posting rubbish to a public address of the server (`v2/launches.py:34-40`, the anonymous
  app-start message) are sent to Sentry today. My pick: answer 400, log it, do not report, because
  nobody here can act on a stranger's rubbish; our own app sending something unreadable there would
  still look the same, which is the cost. Agree?
- GitHub, which the update check asks (case 7), is a service we chose but cannot change. When GitHub
  answers 403 (rate limit) the app says "Couldn't reach GitHub", which is untrue. My pick: treat
  GitHub like a service the person chose: tell the truth ("GitHub says: …", using the form from the
  first decision), do not report; a list we cannot read stays ours and is reported. Agree?

## Not touched unless you say so

Case 27 is JusPrin 1's server code (`web_ent/jusprin/jusprin_cb_views.py`). I am leaving it alone. Do
you want it fixed?

through the real ASGI application (routing, sign-in, credits, real Redis), with
a fake provider that answers the way Anthropic and OpenAI document, and a
stand-in Sentry on this machine that receives what the real Sentry SDK sends.

A chat too large or too long for the provider is the one provider failure the
person can do something about: it is answered with its own code and words and
reaches no Sentry. Every other failure reaches Sentry once, from the one handler at the
top of the endpoint, with the provider's status, request id and error text
and what is known of the request, and the app is told only "Something went

                self.send_response(200)
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(b'{}')

            def log_message(self, *args):
                pass

        self.server = HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), Handler)
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        self.dsn = f'http://publickey@127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_port}/16'

    def close(self):

class FailureTestCase(GatewayTestCase):
    """GatewayTestCase with a stand-in Sentry and a record of every Langfuse
    generation and every kept chat."""

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.sentry = FakeSentry()
        previous = sentry_sdk.get_client()
        sentry_sdk.init(dsn=self.sentry.dsn, default_integrations=False, send_client_reports=False,
                        auto_session_tracking=False)
        self.addCleanup(self.sentry.close)
        self.addCleanup(lambda: sentry_sdk.get_global_scope().set_client(previous))
        self.addCleanup(sentry_sdk.flush)
        patch_attr(self, gateway.os, 'environ', {**gateway.os.environ, 'LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY': 'pk-test'})
        self.langfuse = patch_attr(self, gateway, 'get_client', mock.MagicMock())
        self.kept = patch_attr(self, gateway._Turn, '_keep_sync', mock.MagicMock())

    def events(self):
        """The events that reached the stand-in Sentry."""
        sentry_sdk.flush()
        events = []
        for _, headers, body in self.sentry.received:
            if headers.get('Content-Encoding') == 'gzip':
                body = gzip.decompress(body)
            elif headers.get('Content-Encoding') == 'br':
                body = brotli.decompress(body)
            events += [item.payload.json for item in Envelope.deserialize(body).items if item.type == 'event']
        return events

    def reported(self):
        """The one report, as one line: the exception's type and text."""
        events = self.events()
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 1, events)
        exception = events[0]['exception']['values'][-1]
        return f'{exception["type"]}: {exception["value"]}'

    def outcomes(self):
        return [call.kwargs['metadata']['outcome'] for call in self.langfuse.return_value.start_observation.call_args_list]

    def counted(self):
        return [call.kwargs for call in self.langfuse.return_value.start_observation.call_args_list]

    async def post_chat(self, path, body, **kwargs):
        with override_settings(JUSPRIN_V2_CAPTURE_CONTAINER='jusprin-chats'):
            return await self.post(path, body, chat=CHAT, **kwargs)

    def assert_unexpected_answer(self, response):
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 500, response.text)
        self.assertEqual(response.json(), UNEXPECTED_ANSWER)
        self.assertNotIn(REQUEST_ID, response.text)

    def assert_unexpected_event(self, response):
        """A stream whose last event is the gateway's unexpected answer."""
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        last = parse_sse(response.text)[-1]
        self.assertEqual(last['type'], 'error')
        code = last['error']['code'] if 'error' in last else last['code']
        message = last['error']['message'] if 'error' in last else last['message']
        self.assertEqual((code, message), ('server_error', 'Something went wrong on our side'))


class ProviderRefusalTests(FailureTestCase):
    """Finding 6: a refusal by the provider."""

    async def test_an_anthropic_400_reaches_sentry_with_its_status_request_id_and_text(self):
        self.upstream.status, self.upstream.body = 400, ANTHROPIC_400
        self.upstream.headers = {'content-type': 'application/json', 'request-id': REQUEST_ID}
        response = await self.post_chat('messages', messages_body())
        self.assert_unexpected_answer(response)
        report = self.reported()
        self.assertIn('400', report)
        self.assertIn(REQUEST_ID, report)
        self.assertIn(ANTHROPIC_400_TEXT, report)
        self.assertEqual(self.outcomes(), ['failed UpstreamRefused'])
        self.kept.assert_not_called()

    async def test_an_openai_404_reaches_sentry_with_its_status_request_id_and_text(self):
        self.upstream.status, self.upstream.body = 404, OPENAI_404
        self.upstream.headers = {'content-type': 'application/json', 'x-request-id': REQUEST_ID}
        response = await self.post_chat('responses', responses_body())
        self.assert_unexpected_answer(response)

        self.assertIn(REQUEST_ID, report)

from django.conf import settings
from oauth2_provider.oauth2_backends import get_oauthlib_core
from rest_framework.permissions import SAFE_METHODS


def authenticate(request):
    """The active user whose OAuth2 bearer token the request carries, or None.

    Only a token issued to the JusPrin 2 app counts; another app's token is
    treated as no token at all, so it cannot reach the account or its credits.
    The token needs `read` to read and `write` for anything else, the same rule
    ScopedOAuth2Authentication (obico-server's api/authentication.py) applies
    to the API for apps. A deactivated account's token is refused, and so is a
    token issued to no user.
    """
    scopes = ['read'] if request.method in SAFE_METHODS else ['write']
    valid, oauthlib_request = get_oauthlib_core().verify_request(request, scopes=scopes)
    if not valid or oauthlib_request.access_token.application.client_id != settings.JUSPRIN_V2_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID:
        return None
    user = oauthlib_request.user
    if user is None or not user.is_active:
        return None
    return user

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Builds on [[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]]; used 2026-11-02 when screen control of the app was denied.

- Signed-in conf needs all of: `jusprin_agent.{provider=jusprin, jusprin_api_key, enabled=true, cloud_consent=true, jusprin_model_formats=<JSON id→format from GET /ent/jusprin/v2/models>}`, `jusprin_server.base_url`, `jusprin_onboarding.status=completed`. Without the formats the Agent says "not set up".
- An installed printer is `"models":[{"vendor":"Custom","model":"Generic Klipper Printer","nozzle_diameter":"0.4"}]`, not `vendors`.
- Kill the app before editing the conf. Replace a scratch binary with `rm` then `cp`: `cp` over a binary that has run gets the new process killed at launch.
- `Contents/Resources` in the build is a symlink to the worktree. Replace it with a real folder of links before corrupting a resource, or the worktree gets corrupted.
- Bringing the app forward triggers an account refresh, so to race the gateway (a real 402), change the ledger and send without refocusing.
- Page text input: native value setter plus an `input` event. A modal Preferences window's page polls as `agent-preferences`.
- A test preset needs a `version` field or import rejects it.
- A compose recreate drops env set by a wrapper; check `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` before any chat so only the fake upstream is reachable.

Still needs the screen: pointer hover, native file dialogs, Orca's wizard.

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".
- **A slice right after lldb attaches hung once (2026-11-12).** The worker sat in upstream `name_tbb_thread_pool_threads_set_locale()`, a barrier every TBB thread must reach, and the main thread waited in `BackgroundSlicingProcess::start()` forever. After a relaunch with no debugger the same slice ran at once. Suspected trigger: pausing the app while its thread pool was starting. Don't report such a hang as an app bug without a run that had no debugger attached.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot

"""Per-turn admission: rate limit, then the turn's charge in the credit ledger.

A turn is everything the client sends for one reply, including tool-call
follow-ups; every request of it carries the same X-JusPrin-Turn value. A turn
pays its model's price once, however many requests it makes. Title requests are
free, and a request of kind "note" is a turn the app started, not the person.

The reply requests of one turn are sequential (a follow-up is built from the
previous answer), so the charge does not guard against two reply requests of
the same turn racing each other.
"""
import enum
import time

from django.conf import settings

from jusprin.ledger.ledger import charge_turn
from jusprin.ledger.models import CreditCharge
from lib.cache import REDIS

KEY_PREFIX = 'jusprin:v2'
TURN_TTL_SECONDS = 60 * 60


class Admission(enum.Enum):
    ADMITTED = 'admitted'
    RATE_LIMITED = 'rate_limited'


def admit(user_id: int, turn_id: str, request_kind: str, alias, chat_id: str = None) -> Admission:
    """Count a new turn against the rate limit, then charge it once unless it
    is a title. Raises ledger.CreditsExhausted when it cannot be paid.
    Synchronous: Redis and the credit tables are both blocking."""
    seen_key = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:seen:{user_id}:{turn_id}'
    if REDIS.set(seen_key, '1', nx=True, ex=TURN_TTL_SECONDS):
        bucket = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:turns:{user_id}:{int(time.time() // 60)}'
        pipe = REDIS.pipeline()
        pipe.incr(bucket)
        pipe.expire(bucket, 120)
        turns_this_minute, _ = pipe.execute()
        if turns_this_minute > settings.JUSPRIN_V2_TURNS_PER_MINUTE:
            # The turn was not admitted, so its retry is a new turn again.
            REDIS.delete(seen_key)
            return Admission.RATE_LIMITED

    if request_kind == 'title':
        return Admission.ADMITTED

    charged_key = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:charged:{user_id}:{turn_id}'
    if not REDIS.set(charged_key, '1', nx=True, ex=TURN_TTL_SECONDS):
        return Admission.ADMITTED
    origin = CreditCharge.APP if request_kind == 'note' else CreditCharge.PERSON

def live_lots(user_id: int, now: datetime):
    """The lots still counting, in draw order: the soonest to expire first,
    never-expiring last, oldest first within one expiry."""
    return (CreditGrant.objects
            .filter(Q(expires_at__isnull=True) | Q(expires_at__gt=now), user_id=user_id)
            .order_by(F('expires_at').asc(nulls_last=True), 'created_at', 'id'))


def lock_person(user_id: int) -> None:
    """Serialises everything that spends a person's lots, until the transaction
    ends. On the person's row because they may hold no live lot. no_key lets a new
    lot or charge pointing at that row go ahead."""
    get_user_model().objects.select_for_update(no_key=True).only('pk').get(pk=user_id)


def active_v2_plan(user_id: int) -> Optional[JusPrinPlan]:
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user_id=user_id).first()
    if plan is None or not plan.is_active or plan.plan_id not in settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS:
        return None
    return plan


def _price(alias, origin, plan) -> int:
    if origin == CreditCharge.APP:
        return 0
    if alias.tier == CreditCharge.BASIC and plan and settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS[plan.plan_id].get('unlimited_basic'):
        return 0
    return alias.credits


def charge_turn(user_id: int, turn_id: str, alias, origin: str, chat_id: str = None) -> CreditCharge:
    """Charges a turn once, whatever retries its first request. Raises
    CreditsExhausted with nothing written when the lots cannot pay."""
    now = timezone.now()
    ensure_lots(user_id, now)
    with transaction.atomic():
        lock_person(user_id)
        existing = CreditCharge.objects.filter(user_id=user_id, turn_id=turn_id).first()
        if existing is not None:
            return existing

        lots = list(live_lots(user_id, now))
        plan = active_v2_plan(user_id)
        cost = _price(alias, origin, plan)
        balance = sum(lot.credits_remaining for lot in lots)
        if balance < cost:
            raise CreditsExhausted(balance, cost, plan.plan_id if plan else None)

        charge = CreditCharge.objects.create(user_id=user_id, turn_id=turn_id, chat_id=chat_id, alias=alias.id,
                                             tier=alias.tier, credits=cost, origin=origin)
        left = cost
        for lot in lots:
            if left == 0:
                break
            if lot.credits_remaining <= 0:
                continue
            taken = min(left, lot.credits_remaining)
            lot.credits_remaining -= taken
            lot.save(update_fields=['credits_remaining'])
            CreditAllocation.objects.create(charge=charge, grant=lot, credits=taken)
            left -= taken
    return charge

    async def _handle(self, scope, receive, send):
        """The endpoint's one top handler. A failure nothing expected reaches
        here unchanged: it is reported, and the app is told only that something
        went wrong on our side, as an answer before the reply starts or as the
        stream's last event after. The report carries everything known about
        the request by the time it failed."""
        response = _Response(send)
        facts = {'format': self.fmt}
        unexpected = None
        try:
            async with contextlib.AsyncExitStack() as stack:
                await self._handle_in(scope, receive, response.send, stack, facts)
        except Exception as e:
            unexpected = e
            facts['failure'] = f'{type(e).__name__}: {e}'
            sentry_sdk.capture_exception(e, contexts={'jusprin_request': facts})
            await response.end_unexpectedly(self.fmt)
        # Every request that failed, expected or unexpected, as the place that
        # decided it recorded it in the facts: the log keeps it as well as the
        # report.
        if 'failure' in facts:
            LOGGER.log(logging.ERROR if unexpected else logging.INFO, 'JusPrin v2 gateway request failed; request %s', facts,
                       exc_info=unexpected)

    async def _handle_in(self, scope, receive, send, stack, facts):
        try:
            if scope['method'] != 'POST':
                raise GatewayError(405, 'method_not_allowed')
            # Before the sign-in: a release the server no longer serves is told
            # to update whether or not its sign-in is still good.
            outdated = app_version.refusal(_headers(scope).get('user-agent', ''))
            if outdated is not None:
                raise outdated
            user = await sync_to_async(_authenticate_scope, thread_sensitive=True)(scope)
            if user is None:
                raise GatewayError(401, 'unauthorized')
            headers = _headers(scope)
            turn_id = headers.get('x-jusprin-turn', '')
            request_kind = headers.get('x-jusprin-request', '')
            chat_id = headers.get('x-jusprin-chat')
            facts.update(user_id=user.id, turn_id=turn_id, request_kind=request_kind, chat_id=chat_id,
                         app=headers.get('user-agent'), request_bytes=headers.get('content-length'))
            if not TURN_ID.match(turn_id):
                raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The X-JusPrin-Turn header is missing or not valid.')
            if request_kind not in REQUEST_KINDS:
                raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The X-JusPrin-Request header must be reply, title or note.')
            if chat_id is not None and not capture.CHAT_ID.match(chat_id):
                raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The X-JusPrin-Chat header must be 32 lowercase hex digits.')
            large = await stack.enter_async_context(_large_request_slot(scope))
            raw_body = await _read_body(receive, settings.JUSPRIN_V2_MAX_BODY_BYTES)
            if raw_body is None:
                return  # the client left before sending the whole body
            if large or len(raw_body) > settings.JUSPRIN_V2_LARGE_BODY_BYTES:
                # Parsing and re-encoding megabytes of JSON takes long enough
                # to stall every websocket this process serves.
                upstream = await asyncio.to_thread(prepare, self.fmt, raw_body, get_aliases(), user.id)
            else:
                upstream = prepare(self.fmt, raw_body, get_aliases(), user.id)
            del raw_body
            facts.update(alias=upstream.alias.id, upstream_model=upstream.backend.model, effort=upstream.effort)
            try:
                admission = await sync_to_async(admit, thread_sensitive=True)(
                    user.id, turn_id, request_kind, upstream.alias, chat_id)
            except CreditsExhausted as e:
                raise credits_exhausted(e.cost, e.balance, e.details())
            if admission is Admission.RATE_LIMITED:
                raise GatewayError(429, 'rate_limited')

            # Billing and usage can name the chat; optional, and older apps
            # don't send it. The app encodes it, so one that is not UTF-8 is
            # unexpected.
            title = headers.get('x-jusprin-chat-title')

                    user.id, chat_id, _chat_title(title))
        except GatewayError as e:

            # person's numbers.
            facts['failure'] = f'answered {e.status} {e.code}'
            await _send_error(send, e)
            return

        # back now instead of holding one per open stream.
        await sync_to_async(_release_connection, thread_sensitive=True)()

        # Titles are not part of the chat.
        keep = request_kind != 'title' and capture.enabled()
        turn = _Turn(self.fmt, upstream, user.id, turn_id, request_kind,
                     capture.chat_key(chat_id, turn_id) if keep else None, chat_id)
        relay = asyncio.ensure_future(turn.relay(send))
        disconnect = asyncio.ensure_future(_wait_for_disconnect(receive))
        await asyncio.wait({relay, disconnect}, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
        if relay.done():
            disconnect.cancel()
            facts.update(outcome=turn.outcome, upstream_request_id=turn.request_id)
            if turn.too_large is not None:
                facts['failure'] = f'answered request_too_large: the provider {turn.too_large}'

        else:

            relay.cancel()
            await asyncio.wait({relay})
