  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).

class TokenStrategy(SessionTokenStrategy):
    """allauth's session tokens while the app signs in; once signed in, a new
    access and refresh token for the JusPrin 2 application, issued and saved by
    the same django-oauth-toolkit server and validator as its token endpoint."""

    def create_access_token_payload(self, request):
        server = oauth2_settings.OAUTH2_SERVER_CLASS(oauth2_settings.OAUTH2_VALIDATOR_CLASS(),
                                                     **oauth2_settings.server_kwargs)
        oauth_request = OAuthRequest(request.build_absolute_uri(), http_method='POST')
        oauth_request.user = request.user
        oauth_request.client = Application.objects.get(client_id=settings.JUSPRIN_V2_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID)
        oauth_request.scopes = SCOPE.split()
        oauth_request.grant_type = 'authorization_code'
        token = server.default_token_type.create_token(oauth_request, refresh_token=True)
        server.request_validator.save_bearer_token(token, oauth_request)
        return token


class SyndicateRequestLoginCodeInput(RequestLoginCodeInput):
    def clean_email(self):
        # RequestLoginCodeForm.clean_email, with the account looked up in the
        # request's syndicate and an inactive one refused rather than
        # passed over, so no second account is made beside it.
        email = self.cleaned_data['email']
        if not email:
            return email
        request = context.request
        if not ratelimit.consume(request, action='request_login_code', key=email.lower()):
            raise get_adapter().validation_error('too_many_login_attempts')
        users = users_by_email(email, syndicate_from_request(request))
        if users and not any(user.is_active for user in users):
            raise get_adapter().validation_error('account_inactive')
        active = [user for user in users if user.is_active]
        self._user = active[0] if active else None
        return email


class RequestLoginCodeView(headless.RequestLoginCodeView):
    input_class = SyndicateRequestLoginCodeInput

    def post(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        if self.input._user is None:
            self.input._user = _new_account(request, self.input.cleaned_data['email'])
        return super().post(request, *args, **kwargs)


def _new_account(request, email: str):
    """Makes the account for an address that has none, as the website's sign-up
    does (the account adapter, then the address as an unverified primary
    EmailAddress), with no usable password. Confirming the code verifies the
    address."""
    adapter = get_adapter(request)
    with transaction.atomic():
        user = adapter.new_user(request)
        user.email = email
        user.syndicate = syndicate_from_request(request)
        adapter.populate_username(request, user)
        user.set_unusable_password()
        user.save()
        setup_user_email(request, user, [EmailAddress(email=email)])
    signals.user_signed_up.send(sender=User, request=request, user=user)

    """"Visa ending 4242", or None when Chargebee has no card for the account.
    Asked only of an account that has paid, so Chargebee has its customer; a
    failure to answer is ours, never "no card"."""
    card = chargebee.Customer.retrieve(customer_id(user), env=_site()).card
    if card is None:
        return None
    # Translators: A payment card, as in "Visa ending 4242".
    return _('%(card)s ending %(last4)s') % {
        'card': card.card_type.replace('_', ' ').title() if card.card_type else _('Card'), 'last4': card.last4}


def end_plan_now(plan: JusPrinPlan) -> None:
    """Ends the plan now rather than at the end of its term, for a deleted
    account. A subscription Chargebee cannot find is ours to look at: it may
    have been deleted there, or live on a site this server no longer reads and
    still bill the person, and the answer cannot tell which."""
    status = chargebee.Subscription.retrieve(plan.external_id, env=_site()).subscription.status
    if status != 'cancelled':

def _jusprin_plan_owner(cb_event):
    """The account a JusPrin subscription event is about: by subscription ID
    first, then by the customer's email. A paid subscription that matches no
    account here would never reach its owner, so that is ours to look at,
    even when it turns out to be Chargebee's test event."""
    cb_sub = cb_event['content']['subscription']
    try:
        return JusPrinPlan.objects.get(external_id=cb_sub['id']).user
    except JusPrinPlan.DoesNotExist:
        pass
    try:
        return User.objects.get(email__iexact=cb_event['content']['customer']['email'])

Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Sat Nov 21 22:14:06 2026 -0800

    Chargebee webhook: acknowledge prepaid DH pack invoices with no Obico account
    
    A prepaid AI Detection Hour Pack keeps a $0 placeholder subscription in
    Chargebee that renews every month, even after the Obico account that
    bought it is deleted (which deletes its PrepaidDHPackPlaceholder). Each
    renewal's invoice_generated event then found neither a placeholder nor a
    user with the customer's email, raised User.DoesNotExist and answered
    500. Chargebee retried each event for about three and a half days and
    then emailed a webhook failure (Sentry OBICO-SERVER-AS7); about 25 such
    subscriptions exist.
    
    The handler now logs the event and answers 200 when no account is found,
    since there is no one to credit. Only "placeholder not found" is caught
    now, instead of every exception. Pro subscriptions with no account still
    raise, because those customers are paying.

def cap_image_size(pic):
    try:
        im = Image.open(pic.file)
    except OSError:  # UnidentifiedImageError, or "Truncated File Read" when the cut is inside the header
        raise ValidationError('Corrupted image.')

    # Image.open only reads the header, and LOAD_TRUNCATED_IMAGES (set above) makes Pillow pad a
    # cut-off JPEG with gray instead of raising. The ML API cannot decode a cut-off JPEG, so a
    # JPEG that does not end with its end-of-image marker must be rejected here.
    if im.format == 'JPEG' and not jpeg_is_complete(pic.file):
        raise ValidationError('Corrupted image.')

    # A JPEG can still have valid headers and an end-of-image marker but no scan data. Decode it
    # fully, as the ML API will, so such a pic is rejected here instead of failing there.
    im = Image.open(pic.file)
    try:
        im.load()
    except OSError:
        raise ValidationError('Corrupted image.')

    if max(im.size) <= 1296:
        pic.file.seek(0)
        return pic

    im.thumbnail((1280, 960), Image.LANCZOS)
    output = io.BytesIO()
    im.save(output, format='JPEG')
    output.seek(0)
    return InMemoryUploadedFile(
        output,
        u"pic",
        'pic',
        pic.content_type,
        len(output.getbuffer()),
        None)

    JPEG_END_OF_IMAGE = b'\xff\xd9'
    file.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)

# Print hosts without a printer

Docker containers that run the real print-host software, for testing the app's
Moonraker and OctoPrint paths: connecting, API keys, status, cameras, and
sending a print. Only the printer boards and the cameras' pictures are
simulated. Bambu printers are covered by the in-process fake instead
([Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md)).

| Address | What answers | Key |
|---|---|---|
| `http://127.0.0.1:7130` | Moonraker on Klipper, trusts every address | none |
| `http://127.0.0.1:7131` | the same Klipper through a second Moonraker | needed; HTTP 401 without it |
| `http://127.0.0.1:5030` | OctoPrint 1.11.2 with its bundled virtual printer | needed; HTTP 403 without it |
| `http://127.0.0.1:7140` | the printers' cameras ([Cameras](#cameras)) | none |

Klipper's board is simulavr, an AVR simulator running Klipper's own firmware,
set up from [prind](https://github.com/mkuf/prind). OctoPrint's printer is its
[Virtual Printer](https://docs.octoprint.org/en/devel/bundledplugins/virtual_printer.html)
plugin, which acts like a Marlin printer on a serial port.

## Start and stop

Needs Docker (Docker Desktop on macOS and Windows).

```bash
docker compose -f tests/printer_hosts/docker-compose.yml up -d
```

The first start builds the simulavr image, which nobody publishes
([simulavr/Dockerfile](simulavr/Dockerfile)): a few minutes, most of it
downloading prind's Klipper tools image (1.6 GB to download, about 5.5 GB on
disk with the built image). Klipper reports `ready` some
seconds after the containers start:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7130/printer/info
```

Print the keys as shell exports (`JP_MOONRAKER_KEY`, `JP_OCTOPRINT_KEY`, and a
wrong one, `JP_BAD_KEY`):

```bash
eval "$(tests/printer_hosts/keys.sh)"
```

OctoPrint's key is fixed in `docker-compose.yml`. Moonraker makes its own key
on first start and keeps it until the volumes are removed. OctoPrint's web page
signs in as `admin` / `jusprin-test`.

```bash
docker compose -f tests/printer_hosts/docker-compose.yml down       # keeps keys and uploaded files
docker compose -f tests/printer_hosts/docker-compose.yml down -v    # back to a first start
```

The simulated board uses most of a CPU core for as long as it runs, so stop the
stack when you are done.

## Connecting a printer in the app

Use a printer that is not made by Bambu Lab, such as the generic Klipper
printer, and give the app an address from the table above, with
Moonraker or OctoPrint as the host type. When the app asks for an API key, type
the one `keys.sh` prints, a wrong one, or none, depending on the case. Each
address answers the way a real host does:

| Address and key | What the app's connection test gets |
|---|---|
| `7130`, no key | accepted; Klipper is ready |
| `7131` or `5030`, no key or a wrong key | refused (HTTP 401 or 403), so the app asks for a key |
| `7131` or `5030`, the right key | accepted |

## States worth testing

- **Ready, printing, paused, cancelled, complete:** send G-code with the app,
  or through the API (`/server/files/upload` with `print=true`,
  `/printer/print/pause`, `/printer/print/cancel`). The simulated Klipper
  board runs at half speed (see [simulavr/Dockerfile](simulavr/Dockerfile)),
  so its prints take twice their estimate: the app's 20 mm cube on the
  generic Klipper printer, estimated at 10 minutes, takes about 20.
  OctoPrint's virtual printer keeps its own pace.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

**The task.** It comes from the parent session local_cd3120f7-030a-4af8-a6d1-28ecae789f1a, through a cross-session message, verbatim:

"Two independent reviewers read your uncommitted change, and it is not ready to land: they found 31 problems, several serious. Please work through them.

Three files are in the shared notes folder (`/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_cd3120f7-030a-4af8-a6d1-28ecae789f1a/`). Read them in this order, in full, before changing anything:
1. `misrouted-failures-review-directions.md`: how to treat the findings, what is already settled for each, and answers to the five questions and six sentences in your final report.
2. `misrouted-failures-review-app.md`: 18 findings in the app change.
3. `misrouted-failures-review-server.md`: 13 findings in the server change.

The most serious, to do first:
- After a save failure of ours, autosave stops for the rest of the run and the header can still say "Saved", so edits are lost. A failure in the background worker is also dropped without a report.
- The File menu, its shortcuts, Open Recent and startup have no reporting handler above the new throws, so a failed export or open may end the app.
- On the server, a turn's charge can be given back after its reply was delivered, by sending the same turn id again with a request that fails.

Two things I told you earlier are corrected in the directions file: autosave must keep trying after a failure of ours, and a rate limit from GitHub is not ours.

Treat each finding as a claim: show it, fix it, show it fixed; if it does not hold, say why with evidence. Do not end your turn to wait or after each group; end it when every finding has an end state, then write one report. Commit nothing and push nothing."

**Directions file, key points.**
- Decide whose a failure is by its cause at the operation that failed.
- Settled per finding: see the earlier summary.
- Chat-restore marker: fix it last, by ending the app mid-restore (not by planting the marker). On start, restore losslessly and report once.
- Kept G-code: report once per run.
- Moonraker: reproduce with Docker and check the card offers key entry.
- Declined renewal: no Time Machine; say so if it can't be made to happen.
- OAuthJob field: with Kenneth. Do not build it.
- Sentences:
  - with Kenneth: the chat too long for the model, and a project open in another window;

**Standing constraints, verbatim where quoted.**
- "Commit nothing and push nothing."
- "Send nothing to a real Sentry project. Spend nothing on real AI services without asking Kenneth first."
- Server work stays uncommitted in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`: "never stage `obico-server`, `.claude/launch.json` or anyone else's untracked files. Do not start a second stack."
- JusPrin edits happen only in the worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/misrouted-failures` (branch `claude/misrouted-failures`). Never write in the main checkout.
- Never fix what you haven't reproduced; show each test failing first.
- Use scratch apps and data folders only. Don't front the scratch app. Don't open Kenneth's browser.
- Write no handling code for a failure of ours. New sentences need Kenneth's approval; do not build them.
- Builds:
  - check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first;
  - use `-- -j4`, one build per directory, never restart a running build;
  - run `perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build . --config Release --target … -- -j4` in the background.
- Delete only your own harness data folders. A safety check refused `rm -rf`; leave that deletion to the user.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
- JusPrin error-handling rules (AGENTS.md):
  - a failure goes to whoever can act on it;
  - ours is reported via `report_unexpected_error` (dialog, or sent when automatic reports are on);
  - `report_if_automatic` is for tool calls only;

  - `ACCOUNT_RATE_LIMITS = {'request_login_code': '20/h/ip,5/h/key'}`;
  - code/request "too many" is a 400 `too_many_login_attempts`;
  - code/confirm: 400 `incorrect_code`, then a 409 after 5 wrong codes;

- Pillow `LOAD_TRUNCATED_IMAGES` is set globally by Obico (lib/utils.py, api/octoprint_views.py, app/tasks.py). `verify()` doesn't decode pixels.
- GitHub REST rate limit: a 403 or 429 with `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0` or `retry-after`.

name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control: in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args and @import failures, the model picker needs page JS, a debugger attach once hung a slice."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-12T18:04:04.144Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".
- **A slice right after lldb attaches hung once (2026-11-12).** The worker sat in upstream `name_tbb_thread_pool_threads_set_locale()`, a barrier every TBB thread must reach, and the main thread waited in `BackgroundSlicingProcess::start()` forever. After a relaunch with no debugger the same slice ran at once. Suspected trigger: pausing the app while its thread pool was starting. Don't report such a hang as an app bug without a run that had no debugger attached.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;

# The two reviews of the misrouted-failures change: what became of each finding (2026-11-25)

Every one of the 31 findings now has an end state. 29 were shown happening and are fixed, with a
test that fails on the reviewed code and passes now. 2 do not hold, with the evidence below.
Nothing is committed or pushed in either repository. The JusPrin work is uncommitted in the
worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/misrouted-failures` (branch
`claude/misrouted-failures`); the server work is uncommitted in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`.

## App findings

1. **A background save that fails for a reason of ours was dropped.** Shown: the shell harness made
   the version writer fail inside its worker thread, and nothing was reported in 30 s. Fixed: a
   failure from any step, the worker's included, reaches the timer's report once per project per
   run (`ProjectAutosave::tick`). Checks `autosave_fault_in_the_worker_is_reported`,
   `autosave_fault_keeps_trying_and_reports_once`.
2. **"Saved" while nothing was saved.** Shown in the same harness mode. Fixed: autosave never stops
   after a failure of ours. Each later attempt is new work from the live model, and the header says
   "Couldn't save" until one succeeds. Check `autosave_fault_saves_by_itself_once_cleared`.
3. **File menu, shortcuts, Open Recent and startup had no reporting handler.** Shown: an export from
   the File menu on the reviewed code ended the harness with a crash (exit 139). Startup did not
   escape (the Home listing already catches and logs). Fixed: the menu commands, their shortcuts,
   the Open Recent list and its items each run under `reported(...)` (`Shell/AppMenus.cpp`). The
   harness now drives the real menu items (`autosave_fault_export_from_the_menu_is_reported`,
   `autosave_fault_open_recent_is_reported`).
4. **An export name not ending in exactly ".3mf" was ours.** Fixed: ".3MF" in any case is accepted,
   and the extension is added when missing, as a save dialog does.
5. **New project and a printer switch refused with no word.** Fixed: the person is told why, with
   the system's words, over the window they pressed in. Check
   `unavailable_storage_new_project_pressed_says_why`.
6. **`refused_by_system` decided by exception type and errno.** Shown with a standalone build of the
   reviewed function. Fixed: whose a system error is now depends on the operation. Only the code that
   writes the person's own work (their projects, an export folder they picked, a file they chose)
   turns the system's error into a `SystemRefusal`, through `persons_storage`, taking the reason from
   the call that failed. Anywhere else, such as the printer facts file, a system error stays ours.
   The words always name the folder.
7. **Causes of the person's outside four errno values went to us.** Fixed by the same change: in the
   person's storage any reason the system gives is theirs (quota, failing or unplugged drive, file
   too large, path too long). Test "a refusal is the person's only where their storage is used,
   whatever the system's reason".
8. **A panel that cannot start was reported again after 20 s and on every Retry.** Shown in the real
   built app (AI page pointed at a dead address): two reports. Fixed: one report per run, logged
   after that. Check `panel_cannot_start_is_reported_once`. **Waiting list:** a Windows computer
   without WebView2. OrcaSlicer's `WebView::CheckWebViewRuntime()` can tell the runtime is missing,
   so that case can get a sentence of its own. It needs your wording and a run on Windows, so
   nothing is built.
9. **Sign-in: "a 429 is the person's only at login". Does not hold.** allauth 65.21.1, which the
   server runs, rate-limits only `login` with a 429. Too many code requests answer 400
   `too_many_login_attempts`. Too many wrong codes answer 400 `incorrect_code`, then 409 once the
   code is spent. The app already routes all three to the person (`CloudAccount.cpp:317-333`). No
   change.
10. **Own key, the "anything else" branches.** Fixed: a 404 is the person's only when the service
    says their key cannot use the model (`model_not_found`, OpenRouter's "No endpoints found").
    OpenAI's "Invalid URL" is ours. An outage that answers with a web page and no words shows the
    existing "could not reach the … service" sentence and is not reported. The `model_not_found`
    test is back.
11. **Update check and GitHub's rate limit.** Fixed as corrected: GitHub's rate limit (403 or 429
    with the limit headers) shares "Couldn't reach GitHub" and is not reported. Other error answers,
    and a list the app cannot read, are ours, reported at most once per run, with IP addresses
    removed from what is sent. Tests of the sorting itself and of the address removal.
12. **A failed Save preset press started an AI turn.** Fixed: no AI turn. A refusal by the system
    shows on the card in the system's words. A failure of ours goes to the click's reporting
    handler. Tests in C++ and in the card's page test.
13. **The preset-written check looked at a path it computed itself.** Fixed: it checks the file the
    preset was really written to (`preset.file`), and the model's text stays English throughout.
    Harness check `preset_save_over_a_detached_preset_is_done` (see the test results).
14. **History cleanup reported after every save.** Fixed: once per run.
15. **`install_printer_profiles` rolled back twice.** Fixed: one roll-back and one message; the import
    still stops on a failure of ours. Check `orca_import_profiles_that_cannot_be_installed_are_ours_once`.
16. **Two failures of ours unreported.** Fixed: the checkpoint at the end of a turn no longer
    swallows a failure of ours, and opening a file says "Something went wrong on our side" with a
    report for one.
17. **The printer form stayed on "Reading this printer's profiles…".** Shown by a test; fixed: the
    form is dropped and the page told before the failure goes up.
18. **Tests that did not test what their names said.** Rewritten so each drives the real write or the
    real menu and fails on the reviewed code. The last full run also found six older agent tests
    that still expected the old rule, where any system error was the person's. They now fake the
    autosave the way it really fails, or make only the folder under test unwritable.

**Interrupted chat restore (from your answers).** Reproduced by ending the harness process at the
instant a real chat restore writes its marker, then starting it again on the same data folder. On
the reviewed code the project was missing from Home and could not be opened. Fixed: the store opens
such a project, and opening it finishes the restore without losing anything. If the model had
already moved to the chat's version, that chat is made active. If not, the project stays as it
was before the restore. Either way it is reported once. Shown for both ends of the restore and for
the folder the reviewed code could not open (`--chat-restore-interrupt`, `--chat-restore-recover`).

**Kept G-code that changed on disk:** reported once per run when first noticed (`print_history_changed_package_is_reported_once`).

## Server findings

1. **A delivered reply could be refunded by replaying its turn id.** Shown: the replay got the 5
   credits back. Fixed: whether answer text reached the person is stored on the charge itself (two
   new columns, migration `0007_credit_charge_delivered`), and such a turn is never given back.
2. **The app's 120-second limit looked like Stop.** Fixed: a connection that drops before anything
   was delivered is given back, whoever dropped it. Reproduced with a stalling provider stand-in.
3. **Paid account with no customer on JusPrin 2's site: a 500.** Shown, fixed: "customer not found"
   means no card line; any other failure is ours.
4. **Checkout without a signed-in browser.** Fixed: a log line, back to the prices, no report.
5. **The return address requested without an id.** Fixed: back to the prices, no report.
6. **Back from paying without the sign-in.** Fixed: the existing "open this page from JusPrin"
   page, a log line, no report.
7. **Deletion stops when Chargebee cannot find the subscription.** Kept, and the report now names
   the account and the subscription, so one of us can end it by hand. Kenneth is to be told of this
   change.
8. **JusPrin 1 webhook raising for "no plan and no account".** Found: an ordinary first purchase can
   reach it, when the payment event comes before the browser returns and the address differs. That
   path now answers 503 within an hour of the event, so Chargebee retries, with a log line and no
   report. After that it is ours.
9. **Account lookup by email across products.** Reproduced and fixed: only Obico accounts are looked
   up, so a JusPrin 2 account with the same address is never matched.
10. **A turn that delivered only tool calls was charged.** Fixed: given back when it fails before any
    answer text.
11. **Refund after the report.** Fixed: credits go back first, and the report says they were.
12. **A replay test that passed on the old code.** Rewritten; it fails on the old code.
13. **A cut-off photo passed only because it was 8×8.** Fixed: a real 640×480 photo cut in half.
    Pillow accepts cut-off pictures app-wide here (`LOAD_TRUNCATED_IMAGES`), so the check reuses
    Obico's own JPEG completeness check and then decodes for real.

## Tests at the end

TESTS

## For you to do or decide

- **Sentences still waiting:** the chat too long for the model, a project open in another JusPrin
  window (both with Kenneth); a Windows computer without WebView2 (waiting list, finding 8).
- **Not reproduced:** the Moonraker printer that needs an API key. The Docker Moonraker refuses
  without the key, and the connection test asks for one, but the printer card in the running app
  was not driven. A declined renewal could not be made to happen without Chargebee's Time Machine,
  which is shared, so it was left.
- **Migration** `0007_credit_charge_delivered` is applied to the local server's database.
- **Folders left to delete** (a safety check refused `rm -rf`): harness data folders under
  `/var/folders/6y/fn1z996148dc7xjy2mxx5wkc0000gp/T/` named jusprin-shell-1887-3607-4a95,
  -25e7-202f-fe5c, -6705-0969-eba9, -71ed-f697-b3b0, -7a9e-5c5b-a293, -9138-05c6-f6ac,
  -a188-8bc6-9e8a, -ac57-883f-c336, -c6de-0236-3079, -dfbd-ddf4-728a, -f0ef-7e82-d723,
  -7049-996d-5921, -b080-570b-140e, -48e7-d0f6-28b0, -d217-da83-109f, -8704-aa3c-7059,
  -219d-a2e1-3e38, -1850-2913-b5e2, -8fb1-1d36-e78a, and RUNDIRS.

## Follow-ups found on the way, not fixed

can crash: `~GLCanvas3D → reset_volumes → Selection::clear →
Plater::canvas3D()` dereferences the already-destroyed `Plater::priv`

identical signature exist from 2026-08-28, before the Phase 1 shell change,
so treat it as inherited upstream teardown fragility, not a regression. GUI
test harnesses (tests/workspace, tests/shell) end their scenarios on an empty
project (`new_project`) to avoid tripping it. A real fix belongs in upstream
teardown ordering.

41. Server: the AI provider fails after the message was charged. `v2/credits.py:55`, `ledger/ledger.py:123`, `v2/gateway.py:191-195`. The person is told "our side" and we get a report, but the charge stands and Billing and usage counts the message. No code gives credits back. Checked. - Whether work that failed must be undone (case 41).
- Whether a failure retold by the AI model, or handed to an outside AI client, counts as reaching the person (cases 18, 19, 20).

# Each misrouted failure: a simple change, or more (2026-11-25)

Read only, on the app at `jusprin-dev` `9f485c3604` and the server at `master` `d9c224e114`. Nothing
was changed, built or run for this file. Each place in `error-handling-misrouted-failures.md` has one
entry, except the two Kenneth marked "Not to be fixed": the 120-second limit on a reply, and a
checkout that returns "succeeded" with the invoice unpaid. The list's place 21 holds seven separate
spots, and its places 26 and 27 hold two and four. Each of those spots has its own entry, so there are
50 entries in all. App paths are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, server paths under `web_ent/jusprin/`.

"Simple" here is the reading in the brief, not Kenneth's wording. The change is made at the place
itself by adding or removing a try/catch or an if/else, or by deleting handling. It uses only what the
code has today.

## Counts

- **Simple: 17.**
- **Needs more: 30.**
- **Nothing to change: 3.**
- **Never made to happen: 34.** This counts across the three groups above. It means the failure
  itself was never produced against the real thing, by me or in the evidence I have. A test with a
  fake counts as never made to happen.

The most common reasons a place needs more:
- the person's failure can only be told to them with words we do not have: a new sentence, or the
  "the system says" frame that went with the reversal;
- the failure repeats, every few seconds or on every press, so reporting it once needs a record of
  what was already reported;
- the page or callback gets only "worked or not", so telling "ours" apart from "no network" needs a
  new field.

## The app

**Credits and plans, Billing and usage, will not open.**
- Where: `Shell/ServerSheet.cpp:86-96`, the answer to the link request. Any answer other than 200 with a
  link, or no answer, shows "Couldn't load Credits and plans" (`:375`) with "Check your internet
  connection, then try again."
- Whose: an error answer from our server is ours, and no answer is the person's network. An ended
  sign-in (401) is the person's. Never made to happen.
- Change: throw on an error answer inside the existing `reported(...)` callback, and keep the sentence
  for no answer.
- **Needs more.** The callback hands the sheet only a link or nothing, so the sheet cannot show "ours",
  and it cannot show the existing "sign in again" sentence for the 401. Either needs a new outcome
  carried to the sheet.

**Email sign-in: a refusal the app has no branch for.**
- Where: `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:313-314`. Any 4xx without a branch, and no answer, both show
  "JusPrin couldn't sign you in. Try again."
- Whose: no answer is the person's network. A 4xx from our own server that the app does not expect is
  ours, since our code is on both ends. The local server (allauth 65.21.1) answered a probe like this:
  - a correct password for an address not yet confirmed: 401 with the sign-in flows;
  - too many tries at login: 429;
  - a code request for a deactivated account: 400 `account_inactive`.

  The 401 and the 400 reach this branch today. The probe ran inside a transaction that was rolled
  back, and no email was sent. The app's own display of these was not driven.
- Change: one else-if, so a 4xx with no branch goes to the existing `unexpected(said)`.
- **Needs more.** Two of those answers are the person's and have no sentence: an address not yet
  confirmed (the 401), and a deactivated account. After the change they would be reported as ours.

**Password sign-in: any 400 is "That password is wrong."**
- Where: `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:311-312`.
- Whose: the probe above answered 400 `username_password_mismatch` for a wrong password, for an
  unknown address and for an account with no password, and 400 `too_many_login_attempts` after five
  tries. Both are the person's, and the app has sentences for both. Any other 400 at login is ours.
- Change: an else-if on `username_password_mismatch`, keeping the existing too-many-tries branch and
  sending any other 400 to `unexpected(said)`.
- **Simple.**

**Delete account.**
- Where: `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:143-163`. Any answer but 204 hands the page `false`, and the page
  shows "The account couldn't be deleted. Check your internet connection, then try again."
  (`AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:310`).
- Whose: an error answer from our server is ours, and no answer is the person's network. Never made to
  happen.
- Change: throw on an error answer inside the existing `reported(...)` callback.
- **Needs more.** The page gets only true or false, so it would still show the internet sentence under
  the report. Telling the two apart needs a new field in the answer to the page.

**Print report with no answer.**
- Where: `Home/PrintHistory.cpp:254-258`. Every answer the app does not expect is already thrown. Only
  "no answer at all" keeps the form's "check your connection" sentence.
- Whose: settled by Kenneth's "This error msg is reasonable", which covers a message shown when
  nothing answered.
- **Nothing to change.**

**Update check.**
- Where: `Updates/UpdateCheck.cpp:102-115` and `:126-136`. Any answer but 200, no answer, and a list
  the app cannot read all record a failure, shown as "Couldn't reach GitHub".
- Whose: GitHub's rate limit leaves the person doing the same as no network. Other error answers and
  an unreadable list are ours. GitHub's limit facts are from its documentation, not run.
- Change: throw inside the existing `reported(...)` callback for an error answer that is not the rate
  limit.
- **Needs more.** Two things are missing:
  - the check runs again on a timer and from the Check now button, so the report needs a record of
    "already reported in this run";
  - GitHub's error text names the person's IP address, so it cannot go into the report as it is.

**The AI panel will not start.**
- Where: `Agent/AgentWebView.cpp:237-241, :322-332, :385`. "The AI panel could not connect", with the
  reason and "Bridge traffic: …". It is logged only.
- Whose: a page that does not load or finish its handshake is ours. A Windows computer without WebView2
  is the person's. I made the panel fail in the real built app by pointing the page at a dead address.
- Change: report from `show_bridge_error`.
- **Needs more.** In that run the handshake timer fired again 20 s later, and Retry fires it again, so
  reporting once needs a record. A missing WebView2 needs its own sentence and a way to tell that
  the runtime is missing.

**Home will not start.**
- Where: `Home/HomeWebView.cpp:80, :85, :177`. Three sentences, all logged only.
- Whose: a packaged page missing from the build (`:80`) is ours, and so is a local page that fails to
  load (`:177`). "The system web view could not be created" (`:85`) may be a missing WebView2, which
  is the person's. Never made to happen.
- Change: `report_unexpected_error` at `:80` and `:177`.
- **Needs more**, for `:85` only: a missing WebView2 needs its own sentence. The other two lines are
  simple.

**JusPrin's model list.**
- Where: `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:52-61` with `model_list_fault` (`Agent/ModelCatalog.cpp:196-202`).
  A 4xx from our server, or no answer, shows "Signed in · AI unavailable … Try again in a moment".
  Only a 5xx is reported.
- Whose: a 4xx from our own server is ours, apart from an ended sign-in and the "update the app"
  answer, which already have handling. No answer is the person's network. Never made to happen.
- Change: one if at the call site, for an account profile only. A 4xx that is not a 401 and not an
  update answer throws.
- **Simple.**

**Browser sign-in does not finish.**
- Where: `Agent/CloudSignInMachine.cpp:91-104` and `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:340-342`. "Signing in didn't
  finish. Nothing was saved. Try again." It is logged only.
- Whose: made to happen with probes against OrcaSlicer's sign-in job.
  - A port another program holds gives "bind: Address already in use", which is the person's.
  - Our token exchange answering 400, answering 500, or not running at all gives the same "Unknown
    error" in all three cases. Those three are ours.
  - The person declining in the browser gives a different message, and that one is the person's.
- **Needs more.** The three that are ours cannot be told from one another, or from other failures,
  without a field in OrcaSlicer's `OAuthJob` result. That is an OrcaSlicer-owned file, and the field
  is with Kenneth.

**Autosave.**
- Where: `Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:351` and `Shell/StatusRow.cpp:616`. Disk full, a folder that
  cannot be written, and our own bug all show "Changes couldn't be saved. JusPrin will retry.", and the
  system's reason is dropped.
- Whose: the system refusing to write the person's projects folder is theirs. Anything else is ours.
  Made to happen in the shell harness, with a full projects folder, one that cannot be written, and a
  failing writer.
- **Needs more.** The person's case needs the system's words shown with who said them, which needs a
  frame string. The save retries every 2 s, so reporting ours once needs a record per project.

**Export, restore, version history.**
- Where: `Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp:161-168` and its two neighbours. "The project couldn't be exported.
  Try again." and two like it. The reason is logged only.
- Whose: a folder the person picked that the system refuses is theirs. Anything else is ours. Made to
  happen in the harness, from the real File menu.
- Change: rethrow for anything but the system's refusal.
- **Needs more.** The person's case needs the system's words and a frame string.

**Opening a project.**
- Where: `Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:952-954`. The same "The project couldn't be opened. Try again."
  covers three owners.
- Whose:
  - a project another JusPrin window holds is the person's;
  - the current project failing to save because the system refused is the person's;
  - a damaged project is ours.

  All three were made to happen in the harness.
- **Needs more.** The other-window sentence is with Kenneth. The system's refusal needs the frame
  string. Only the damaged project, which would be a rethrow, is simple.

**A project with an interrupted chat restore disappears from Home.**
- Where: `Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:444`. The store refuses a project whose restore marker is
  still there ("requires recovery"), and the project is missing from Home and cannot be opened.
- Whose: ours. Made to happen by ending the app at the instant a real restore wrote its marker, then
  starting it again.
- **Needs more.** Deleting the refusal opens the project, but the open chat and the model can be on
  different versions. Making them match again needs new code that finishes the restore.

**The projects folder cannot be read.**
- Where: `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1019`. "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying."
  The reason is dropped.
- Whose: the system refusing the person's folder is theirs. Anything else is ours. Made to happen at
  startup with the projects folder replaced by a plain file.
- **Needs more.** The person's case needs the frame string. The listing runs every second, so
  reporting ours once needs a record.

**Printer profiles shipped with the app fail to install or read.**
- Where:
  - `Home/OrcaImporter.cpp:229-231`: logged only;
  - `:341-345`: a printer is marked "JusPrin couldn't load this preset";
  - `PrinterSetup/SetupOptionsLoader.cpp:83-86`: shown as "The printer profiles could not be read: …".
- Whose: ours. The code's own comment says this fails only on a broken install. Made to happen in the
  harness with profiles that cannot be installed.
- Change: throw at each of the three spots in place of the log line or the marked reason.
- **Simple.**

**Save on a proposal card.**
- Where: `AgentUI/src/components/ProposalCard.tsx:31-32`. "The action failed.", and the failure goes to
  the AI as a tool result.
- Whose: the system refusing the preset file is the person's. Anything else is ours. Only made to
  happen with fakes, in C++ and page tests.
- **Needs more.** The card gets only the tool's state. Showing the system's words needs a field and the
  frame string, and reporting ours needs the press handled as the person's click, not as a tool call.

**Tool failures in the app's own work reach us only with automatic reports on.**
- Where: `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:714-717`.
- Whose: this is the rule's own exception. AGENTS.md says such a failure is reported "only if the
  person has turned automatic reports on".
- **Nothing to change.**

**The local tool server's helper tells the outside AI client to open JusPrin when JusPrin is open.**

- Whose: ours. The settled answer is that the helper tells the client the truth and logs, with no

- Change: an else-if that hands the client the error JusPrin itself sent, in place of the offline

**History cleanup warning.**
- Where: `Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:455`. Logged only.
- Whose: ours. Never made to happen against the real store.

    async def _handle(self, scope, receive, send):

        went wrong on our side, as an answer before the reply starts or as the
        stream's last event after. The report carries everything known about

    term, then deletes the account, and with it its credits, tokens and kept

metadata:

---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".
- **A slice right after lldb attaches hung once (2026-11-12).** The worker sat in upstream `name_tbb_thread_pool_threads_set_locale()`, a barrier every TBB thread must reach, and the main thread waited in `BackgroundSlicingProcess::start()` forever. After a relaunch with no debugger the same slice ran at once. Suspected trigger: pausing the app while its thread pool was starting. Don't report such a hang as an app bug without a run that had no debugger attached.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

The search turned up OpenRouter's documentation on typed errors, and it supports the core of your query.

- **`error_type` is the field to key on.** OpenRouter's docs say native codes such as Anthropic's `error.type` are best-effort and can differ by format, so `error_type` is the more reliable signal across formats. (https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/errors-and-debugging.md)
- **Where it appears on mid-stream errors.** On Chat Completions, the typed code sits at `error.metadata.error_type` in the SSE error chunk. (https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/errors)
- **Stream termination.** The stream-error chunk includes a `choices` entry with `finish_reason: "error"`, and the HTTP status stays 200 because headers were already sent. The stream then ends. (https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/errors)
- **Why there's no failover mid-stream.** Once partial output has reached the client, OpenRouter cannot switch providers without duplicating or corrupting the answer. (https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/errors)
- **Overload timing.** A provider overload that happens after streaming has started is classed as a mid-stream error. Errors before any tokens are sent can still be retried on a backup provider. (https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/errors-and-debugging)
- **500-class masking.** For 500s, the message is replaced with a generic string and `provider_code` is dropped, but `error_type` remains (value `server`). (https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/errors)
- **Valid values.** The documented enum includes `provider_overloaded` and `provider_unavailable`, among others such as `rate_limit_exceeded` and `invalid_request`. The enum is open, so unrecognized values should be tolerated. (https://openrouter.ai/docs/client-sdks/python/components/apierrortype.md)

# The 17 simple changes to misrouted failures (2026-11-25)

Kenneth approved the 17 places that `misrouted-failures-simple-or-not.md` calls simple, each only after
its failure has been made to happen ("Yes, the 17"). This file has one entry per place. Each changed
place says what happened before the change, the change itself, what happened after, which handler
reports it, and whether a person can get there by doing something ordinary. Each place left untouched
says why.

**Counts.** 6 places changed (3 in the app, 3 on the server). Two of them are changed only in part,
because only some of their spots could be made to happen: billing, and the shipped printer profiles.
11 places are left untouched (5 in the app, 6 on the server).

**Where the work is.** Nothing is committed or pushed.
- App: the worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/misrouted-failures`, branch
  `claude/misrouted-failures`, uncommitted. Full diff: `misrouted-failures-simple-changes-app.patch` in
  this folder.
- Server: `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`, `web_ent/jusprin/`, uncommitted. Full diff:
  `misrouted-failures-simple-changes-server.patch` in this folder.

**How the failures were made to happen.**
- App: a scratch copy of the built app with its own data folder. A local stand-in program answered in
  place of Sentry and, where needed, in place of the AI service, and passed everything else to the
  local server. Every Sentry report the app sent was counted there. Nothing went to a real Sentry
  project, and nothing went to a real AI service.
- Server: the local server over HTTP, signed in with a test account's token. The local server's
  `SENTRY_DSN` is empty, so its 500s go nowhere.
- Evidence folders (logs, page messages, the stand-in's received reports):
  `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/b575a9e5-080c-46d7-b71a-f5842e099a04/scratchpad/live/runs/<name>-before` and `-after`.
  The scratchpad can be cleared by a reboot.

**Tests.**
- Server: all of `jusprin.v2.tests` pass. Each new or changed test was also run on the old code and
  fails there.
- App: `agent_bridge_tests` (648 cases), `jusprin_profile_tests` (20) and `jusprin_tests` (200) all
  pass.

## The app

### Sign out with no network — changed

- **Before.** The local server was reached through a proxy, and the proxy was stopped before signing
  out. The app was then sent the same message Preferences sends for "Sign out". The log said
  "Unexpected error while signing out of JusPrin: … revoking the token at …/o/revoke_token/ answered 0:
  curl:Couldn't connect to server", and 1 report reached the stand-in (run `signout-before`).
- **Change** (`Agent/CloudSignInMachine.cpp`):
  ```diff
               .on_error(reported("signing out of JusPrin", [url](std::string body, std::string error, unsigned status) {
  +                // No answer, such as no network: the token is already
  +                // forgotten on this computer, and nobody can act on it.
  +                if (status == 0) {
  +                    BOOST_LOG_TRIVIAL(warning) << "Signing out of JusPrin reached no server at " << url << ": " << error;
  +                    return;
  +                }
                   // Forgotten on this computer, the token still works on the
                   // server.
                   throw RuntimeError("revoking the token at " + url + " answered " + std::to_string(status) + ": " + error +
  ```
- **After.** Same arrangement. One warning line, "Signing out of JusPrin reached no server at …", and
  0 reports (run `signout-after`). The token is still gone from the app's settings file.
- **Handler.** Any other failure still throws inside `reported("signing out of JusPrin", …)`, which
  reports it.
- **Ordinary person?** Yes: signing out with the network off. That is why no answer at all is now not
  reported. Nothing is shown, as before, because there is nothing for the person to do. An answer the
  server refuses is still ours and still reported.

### Own key: the service is down or overloaded — changed

The change covers three spots: an error answer of 500 or above, an overload or server error named
inside a reply, and the AI models list. It applies only to a profile with the person's own key. It
does not apply to a JusPrin account, where the service is ours, or to a model on this computer.

- **Before.** The app used an OpenRouter profile with a key, and its AI address was pointed at the
  stand-in.
  - A 502 with OpenRouter's own words, "Your chosen model is down…" (run `40-down-before`): the chat
    showed "Something went wrong on our side", and 2 reports were sent.
  - A reply that failed inside the stream with `server_error` / `provider_overloaded` (run
    `40-overloaded-in-reply-before`): the same sentence, and 2 reports.
  - The chat title request failing with 502 after a good reply (run `40-title-down-before`): the log
    said "Unexpected error while making a chat's title", and 1 report was sent.
  - The models list answering 503 (run `40-models-down-before`): 4 reports for 4 failed reads, 2 of
    JusPrin's list and 2 of OpenRouter's.
- **Change** (`Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp`, `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp`):
  ```diff
       if (expected)
           return this->expected(std::move(*expected), answered, words);
  +    // The service of the person's own key failing on its side: whoever runs
  +    // it can fix it, and nobody here can.
  +    if (!m_config.profile.account_sign_in && !m_config.profile.on_this_computer && event.status >= 500)
  +        // TRN %1% is an AI provider, such as OpenAI.
  +        return this->expected({"network_error", Slic3r::format(translated(L("The AI request could not reach the %1% service.")), m_config.profile.display_name), true},
  +                              answered, words);

  ```

  ```diff
   {
  -    if (!m_config.profile.account_sign_in)
  +    if (!m_config.profile.account_sign_in) {
  +        // The service of the person's own key overloaded or failing on its
  +        // side, as Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenRouter name it inside a reply.
  +        const ServiceSays says = service_says(answer);
  +        if (!m_config.profile.on_this_computer &&
  +            (says.type == "overloaded_error" || says.type == "api_error" || says.code == "server_error" ||
  +             says.error_type == "provider_overloaded" || says.error_type == "provider_unavailable" || says.error_type == "server"))
  +            // TRN %1% is an AI provider, such as OpenAI.
  +            return AgentError{"network_error", Slic3r::format(translated(L("The AI request could not reach the %1% service.")), m_config.profile.display_name), true};
           return provider_answer(0, answer);
  +    }
  ```

  ```diff
  +            // The service of the person's own key failing on its side is for
  +            // whoever runs it; the list is marked failed above.
  +            if (!fetch->profile.account_sign_in && !fetch->profile.on_this_computer && status >= 500)
  +                return;
  ```

  The sentence is the one the app already shows when the service cannot be reached. It is an existing
  msgid, so the catalogs do not change. The in-reply names come from each service's documentation:
  Anthropic's `overloaded_error` and `api_error`, OpenAI's `server_error`, and OpenRouter's
  `provider_overloaded`, `provider_unavailable` and `server`.
- **After.** Same arrangements.
  - The 502 and the in-reply failure: "The AI request could not reach the OpenRouter service.", with
    the retry the app offers for that sentence, and 0 reports.
  - The title: the chat stays untitled, and 0 reports.
  - The models list: 2 reports, both for JusPrin's list, whose failure is ours. OpenRouter's 2 are
